site_name: The White House,  Harrow On The Hill Campus  Lowlands Road
description: Change of use of an educational building (Use Class F1a) to a community health hub (Use Class E(e)) comprising GP surgeries and primary healthcare facilities; external alterations including installation of bay window to front elevation, installation of window and door to front elevation; parking; landscaping including footpath works (demolition of conservatory)
decision_conditions: <p>Landscaping</p><p>The development hereby permitted shall not commence until there has been submitted to, and approved by, the local planning authority, a scheme of hard and soft landscape works at a scale not less than 1:100. The hard and soft landscaping scheme shall include the following details:</p><p>- Soft landscape works shall include: planting plans, and schedules of plants, noting species, plant sizes and proposed numbers / densities.</p><p>- Site levels and planting levels</p><p>- Hard landscape works shall include details of any boundary treatment, hard surfacing and lighting of the external areas taking into account of nocturnal animals. The lighting details shall include all external areas (including buildings) within the site, including locations, lighting design, lighting details, specification, elevations, light spillage and lighting levels and would need to take account of any biodiversity recommendations or requirements, such as bat friendly lighting.</p><p>The hard and soft landscaping scheme shall be undertaken in accordance with the approved details and thereafter retained.</p>

<p>Landscape Management Plan</p><p>The development hereby permitted shall not be brought into use, until a scheme for the ongoing management and maintenance of all hard and soft landscaping within the development has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The scheme shall comprise:</p><p>a) A Landscape Management Plan for the whole development, including:</p><p>Long-term landscape design objectives and management aims;</p><p>Management responsibilities, ownership arrangements and maintenance obligations;</p><p>A management programme of works, including any phased implementation;</p><p>Monitoring and review procedures; and measures to ensure the successful establishment, long-term retention and maturation of the approved landscape scheme and all communal outdoor amenity areas.</p><p>b) A Landscape Maintenance Plan covering a minimum period of five years from completion of the landscaping works, including:</p><p>Maintenance schedules and a calendar of routine maintenance operations for all hard and soft landscaped areas;</p><p>Details of watering, weeding, pruning, strimming, litter clearance and other horticultural operations;</p><p>Maintenance of landscape structures and features, including furniture, pergolas, plant supports, raised beds, lighting and other associated landscape infrastructure;</p><p>Procedures for the replacement of failed, damaged or diseased planting; and identification of the party or parties responsible for carrying out all maintenance operations.</p><p>The approved Landscape Management Plan and Landscape Maintenance Plan shall thereafter be implemented and adhered to in full for the lifetime of the development.</p>

<p>Refuse storage</p><p>Notwithstanding the proposed plans, details for the proposed location and design of the bin store demonstrating sufficient number of waste and recycling bins for the use and appropriate access, are to be provided to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority prior to the commencement of the relevant works, including consideration of alternative locations and clear and convincing justification for any heritage harm.</p><p>The refuse storage works shall be carried out in accordance with the approved details and thereafter retained. Other than on collection days, the bins shall be stored at all times within the designated refuse storage area as shown on the approved plans.</p>

<p>Site levels</p><p>No site works or development shall commence until details of the levels of the building(s), road(s) and footpath(s) in relation to the adjoining land and highway(s), and any other changes proposed in the levels of the site, have been submitted to, and approved by, the local planning authority.</p>
<p>Timing</p><p>The development hereby permitted shall be begun before the expiration of three years from the date of the permission.&nbsp;</p>

<p>Material Details</p><p>Notwithstanding the plans hereby approved, details for the following (including existing and proposed scaled plans, elevations and sections to a scale of 1:10 or 1:20 and material details as appropriate) shall be provided to, and approved in writing by, the Local Planning Authority prior to the commencement of the relevant part of the work:</p><p>a) Changes in access to front porch</p><p>b) Bollards</p><p>c) New hard surfacing</p><p>d) The proposed window G06.W01 to the frontage, to match window F08.W01.</p><p>e) The proposed new door to the southern frontage to the proposed dirty utility room.</p><p>f) Materials and details for the front conservatory addition. </p><p>g) Proposed new doors to the north elevation.</p><p>The development shall be undertaken in accordance with the approved details and thereafter retained.</p>

<p>Construction Logistics and Management Plan (CLMP)</p><p>- No development shall commence until a Construction Logistics and Management Plan (CLMP) has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The approved CLMP shall be adhered to throughout the construction period. The CLMP shall include (but not be limited to) the following:</p><p>a. Construction Vehicle Routing and Access.</p><p>- Details of all construction access routes to and from the site, including entry and exit points.</p><p>- Measures to ensure that construction traffic adheres to approved routes.</p><p>b. Loading and Unloading Arrangements. - Identification of designated areas within the site for the loading and unloading of plant, materials, and equipment.</p><p>- Details demonstrating that all loading and unloading activities will take place within the site boundary, unless otherwise agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority.</p><p>- Measures to prevent obstruction of the public highway and surrounding streets.</p><p>c. Protection of Vulnerable Road Users (VRUs).</p><p>- Measures to ensure the safety of pedestrians, cyclists, and other vulnerable road users, including:</p><p>Temporary traffic management arrangements (e.g. signage, barriers, controlled crossings).</p><p>- Use of banksmen or marshals during vehicle movements.</p><p>- Segregation of construction traffic from pedestrian and cycle routes where reasonably practicable.</p><p>- Timing restrictions to avoid peak pedestrian and school travel periods where appropriate.</p><p>d. Construction Traffic Management- Details of delivery times and restrictions to minimise conflict with peak traffic periods.</p><p>- On-site turning facilities to ensure vehicles can enter and exit in a forward gear.</p><p>e. Site Management Measures</p><p>- Wheel washing facilities (if required).- Measures to control mud, dust, and debris on the public highway.</p><p>- Contact details for a site manager responsible for compliance.</p><p>The construction works shall be undertaken in accordance with the approved details for the duration of the works.</p>

<p>Biodiversity Gain Plan</p><p>Notwithstanding the approved details, the development hereby approved shall not commence unless a Biodiversity Gain Plan has been submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. The biodiversity gain plan must include the following (where relevant):</p><p>(a) information about the steps taken or to be taken to minimise the adverse effect of the development on the biodiversity of the onsite habitat and any other habitat;</p><p>(b) the pre-development biodiversity value of the onsite habitat;</p><p>(c) the post-development biodiversity value of the onsite habitat;</p><p>(d) any on-site (within the blue line boundary as shown on the site location plan) registered offsite biodiversity gain allocated to the development and the biodiversity and the biodiversity value of that gain in relation to the development;</p><p>(e) any biodiversity credits purchased for the development; and</p><p>(f) any such other matters as the Secretary of State may by regulations specify.</p>

<p>Habitat Management and Monitoring Plan (HMMP)</p><p>The development hereby approved shall not commence until a Habitat Management and Monitoring Plan (HMMP), prepared in accordance with the Biodiversity Gain Plan, has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. This shall include:</p><p>(a) A non-technical summary;</p><p>(b) The roles and responsibilities of the people or organisation(s) delivering the HMMP;</p><p>(c) The planned habitat creation and enhancement works to create or improve habitat to achieve the biodiversity net gain in accordance with the approved Biodiversity Gain Plan;</p><p>(d) The management measures to maintain habitat in accordance with the approved Biodiversity Gain Plan for a period of 30 years from the completion of development; and</p><p>(e) The monitoring methodology and frequency in respect of the created or enhanced habitat to be submitted to the local planning authority (evidence i.e. site photos taken in Years 1, 3, 5, 10 and every 5 years after Year 10)</p><p>No occupation of the development shall take place until:</p><p>(a) the habitat creation and enhancement works set out in the approved HMMP have been completed; and</p><p>(b) a completion report, evidencing the completed habitat enhancements, has been submitted to, and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority.</p><p>The created and/or enhanced habitat specified in the approved HMMP shall be managed and maintained in accordance with the approved HMMP.</p>

<p>Toolbox talk</p><p>No development shall take place (including demolition, ground works, vegetation clearance etc) until an Ecological Clerk of Works (ECoW) has been appointed, and a programme of ecological toolbox talks has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The talks shall be delivered to all site personnel by the ECoW prior to commencement of works. The talks will cover the sensitivity of protected species, namely bats and nesting birds, as well as ecological features to be retained and precautionary working methods. Evidence of training (signed sheets) shall be submitted to the Council within 14 days of the talk. Should a protected species be found at any point, works should cease, and advice should be sought from a suitably qualified ecologist.</p>

<p>Biodiversity Enhancement Plan</p><p>Prior to the commencement of construction, a scale, colour plan of biodiversity enhancements on the site, to include the number, specification, and location of enhancements such as bat and bird boxes, shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. Thereafter, the biodiversity enhancement measures shall be carried out and retained in accordance with the approved details.</p>

<p>Fire safety statement</p><p>Prior to the commencement of the development hereby approved, a Fire Safety Statement shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority, this statement shall include details of how the development will function in terms of the following:</p><p>1) identify suitably positioned unobstructed outside space:</p><p>a) for fire appliances to be positioned on</p><p>b) appropriate for use as an evacuation assembly point</p><p>2) is designed to incorporate appropriate features which reduce the risk to life and the risk of serious injury in the event of a fire; including appropriate fire alarm systems and passive and active fire safety measures</p><p>3) is constructed in an appropriate way to minimise the risk of fire spread</p><p>4) provide suitable and convenient means of escape, and associated evacuation strategy for all building users</p><p>5) develop a robust management strategy for evacuation which is to be periodically updated and published (details of how often this management strategy is to be reviewed and published to be included), and which all building users can have confidence in</p><p>6) provide suitable access and equipment for firefighting which is appropriate for the size and use of the development.</p><p>The development shall be operated in accordance with the approved details in perpetuity.</p>

<p>Opening hours</p><p>The use hereby permitted shall not be open to customers outside the following times: -</p><p>07:00 hours to 22.00 hours, Monday to Friday inclusive,</p><p>07:30 hours to 22:00 hours Saturday, Sundays &amp; Bank Holidays</p><p>without the prior written permission of the local planning authority.</p>

<p>Tree Protection Plan and Method Statement</p><p>Notwithstanding the approved plans and documents, no site clearance, preparatory work or development shall take place until a scheme for the protection of the retained trees (the tree protection plan) and the appropriate working methods (an arboricultural method statement) in accordance with paragraphs 5.5 and 6.1 of British Standard BS 5837: Trees in relation to design, demolition and construction - Recommendations (or in an equivalent British Standard if replaced) has been submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. The scheme for the protection of the retained trees shall be carried out as approved.</p>

<p>Tree Protection</p><p>The erection of fencing for the protection of any retained tree shall be undertaken in accordance with the approved plans and particulars before any equipment, machinery or materials are brought on to the site for the purposes of the development, and shall be maintained until all equipment, machinery and surplus materials have been removed from the site. Nothing shall be stored or placed in any area fenced in accordance with this condition, and the ground levels within those areas shall not be altered, nor shall any excavation be made, without the written consent of the local planning authority.</p>

<p>Cycle Parking</p><p>Notwithstanding the details hereby approved, prior to the first use of the development, details of the cycle store, internal racks, dimensions and location shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. The cycle storage shall be made available prior to first use of the building and shall be retained thereafter.</p>
